models.name: Model A: Steady RANS Pump Flow Solver (k-ω SST)
models.what_it_computes: Time-averaged 3D velocity, pressure, viscous shear rate, and wall shear distributions throughout the rotating assembly and volute under specified operating points.

models.name: Model B: Eulerian Hemolysis Scalar Transport
models.what_it_computes: An advected hemolysis index field driven by local shear exposure and residence time, yielding volumetric hemoglobin release rate and outlet-averaged hemolysis metrics.

models.name: Model C: Lagrangian Particle Damage Accumulation
models.what_it_computes: Trajectory-resolved residence times and cumulative red-blood-cell damage along pathlines, producing distributions of exposure dose and hotspot identification.

mechanisms.name: M1: Boundary-layer shear on blades and shroud
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Sustained near-wall viscous shear contributes to sublethal and lethal red-cell damage as fluid glides along rotating and stationary surfaces.

mechanisms.name: M2: Tip-leakage and rotor–stator interaction peaks
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Localized high-shear transients in the gap and wake regions generate short-duration but intense stresses implicated in hemolysis bursts.

mechanisms.name: M3: Recirculation-driven residence time in the volute
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Slow-moving zones extend cumulative exposure, amplifying damage even at moderate shear and elevating outlet plasma-free hemoglobin.

deviation.detail: All credibility factors are scored per model–mechanism on a 0–4 scale (0=not met, 1=limited, 2=adequate, 3=strong, 4=compelling) and summarized numerically.

findings.span: Flow rates in the simulations matched the calibrated Coriolis meters within 2% at each operating point, impeller speeds were within 10 rpm of tachometer readings, and fluid properties were set to measured values: 3.5 ± 0.1 mPa·s at 36.5 ± 0.3 °C for blood loops and 3.5 ± 0.05 mPa·s at 22 °C for the transparent model.
Collectively, the alignment of the simulated and tested conditions is within a narrow tolerance in both hydraulic and hemorheologic parameters.
Inlet scalar values for Model B are set to zero, corresponding to fresh blood entering the pump loop after the cooler and upstream tubing.

Tip-gap measurements on the tested pumps established 90 ± 10 µm clearance, and the computational geometries were adjusted to use the measured clearance for each pump where hemolysis data were collected.
Operating conditions, hematocrit, viscosity, and temperature are matched to simulations, and hardware variability is characterized across two manufacturing lots.
Massless particles are released at the pump inlet surface with sampling density proportional to local volumetric flux.

The computational mesh is hybrid unstructured, with polyhedral cells in bulk regions and prismatic layers near walls; mesh sizes range from 8.4 million to 14.7 million cells depending on operating point, refined particularly in the tip gap where minimum gap width is 90 ± 10 micrometers per metrology.
The simulation boundary conditions were set to reproduce the bench settings at each operating point.
Turbulence model constants follow standard k–omega SST values and are not tuned.
For the transparent model used in LDA, dimensional fidelity is verified to within ±0.1 mm on chord and ±0.15 mm on radial positions compared to the production geometry.
The chosen coefficients are C = 3.62e7 (SI units), a = 2.416, and b = 0.785, recognizing that alternative fits exist and produce different predictions.

Sensitivity analysis for Model B is performed at 3.5 L/min, 100 mmHg by bracketing the exponent a between 2.30 and 2.64 and C between 2.9e7 and 4.2e7; the resulting outlet hemolysis flux varies by a factor of 1.8, while the spatial pattern of H is similar.

To implement the source within a steady flow, we compute an effective exposure time at each point using a mean age-of-fluid scalar, which satisfies an additional transport equation with a unit source term.
The particle count is 500,000 per operating point, yielding more than 2.5e8 time steps across the ensemble.
for the present study, a fixed 0.2 ms sliding surrogate is applied to all blade and shroud contacts.

Statistical convergence was verified by doubling the particle count at 3.5 L/min and 100 mmHg, which changed the 99th percentile of E by less than 4% and the fraction of particles exceeding the critical exposure threshold by less than 0.2 percentage points.
